Package org.cyborgcats.component

Class Flywheel

java.lang.Object
org.cyborgcats.component.MotorComponent
org.cyborgcats.component.VelocityComponent
org.cyborgcats.component.Flywheel
All Implemented Interfaces:
Component
public class Flywheel extends VelocityComponent
Extension of VelocityComponent for flywheel-style shooters that blends open-loop spin-up with closed-loop velocity holding.

While the wheel is still below its commanded speed the component runs full duty cycle to reach the setpoint as quickly as possible, then hands off to the motor's closed-loop velocity control once the wheel is at (or above) speed. See getControlType(double, double) for the exact switching rule.

    • Flywheel

      public Flywheel(String name, double epsilon, double debounceTime, MotorIOConfiguration leader, MotorIOConfiguration... followers)
      Constructs a Flywheel.
      Parameters:
      name - unique name used as the AdvantageKit logging key under "mechanisms/"
      epsilon - velocity tolerance used to determine whether the shooter is at a target speed
      debounceTime - how long (in seconds) the shooter must continuously be within epsilon before the at-velocity check returns true
      leader - hardware interface for this motor
      followers - hardware interfaces driven with the same control request as the leader; may be omitted for a single-motor shooter

  • Method Details

    • getControlType

      public Flywheel.ControlType getControlType(double target, double epsilon)
      Chooses the control strategy for the current loop.

      Returns Flywheel.ControlType.VELOCITY when the shooter is already debounced-at-setpoint, or when the measured velocity has reached or passed the setpoint; otherwise returns Flywheel.ControlType.BANGBANG so the wheel keeps spinning up at full output.

      Note: this advances the shared VelocityComponent debouncer via VelocityComponent.nearVelocity(double, double), so calling it more than once per robot loop distorts the debounce timing.

      Parameters:
      target - intended target velocity
      epsilon - velocity tolerance used for the at-setpoint check
      Returns:
      the control type to use this loop

    • applyTargetSetpoint

      public void applyTargetSetpoint(double velocity)
      Computes and immediately applies the setpoint for the given velocity.

      Intended to be called every loop: the control type is re-evaluated each call, so repeated calls carry the shooter from spin-up through steady-state velocity holding.

      Parameters:
      velocity - desired shooter velocity

    • applyTargetSetpointState

      public State applyTargetSetpointState(double velocity)
      Creates a one-shot State that applies the setpoint for the given velocity when scheduled.

      The state runs a single step, so it performs one spin-up/hold decision rather than driving the shooter to speed on its own; schedule it repeatedly (or wrap it) to keep the shooter commanded.

      Parameters:
      velocity - desired shooter velocity
      Returns:
      the newly created state
